title.value: Effects of gene dosage on cognitive ability: A function-based association study across brain and non-brain processes
title.justification: The title is stated at the beginning and gives a clear summary of the study focus.
title.quote: Effects of gene dosage on cognitive ability: A function-based association study across brain and non-brain processes

analysis.description: The paper explores the impact of copy number variants (CNVs) on cognitive abilities, focusing on gene-dosage-sensitive biological processes. The study analyzes CNVs in over 258,000 individuals to understand how deletions and duplications affect cognitive functions, using novel statistical methods to assess the effects across brain and non-brain biological processes.

type.justification: The paper involves a significant amount of data analysis from a large cohort to empirically study the effects of CNVs on cognitive abilities.
type.quote: To investigate this issue, we identified all CNVs >50 kilobases in 258k individuals from 6 general population cohorts with assessments of general cognitive abilities.

name.justification: The study focuses on understanding the genetic basis of cognitive abilities, primarily through the examination of CNVs and gene dosage across multiple cohorts.
name.quote: To investigate this issue, we identified all CNVs >50 kilobases in 258k individuals from 6 general population cohorts with assessments of general cognitive abilities.

name.justification: The paper addresses the impact of CNVs on neurodevelopmental disorders like autism and schizophrenia.
name.quote: CNVs are major contributors to risk for neurodevelopmental disorders, including intellectual disability (ID), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and schizophrenia.

name.justification: The paper develops and employs statistical methods like CNV-GWAS and functional burden analyses.
name.quote: We performed a CNV-GWAS and functional burden analyses, which tested 6502 gene-sets defined by tissue and cell-type transcriptomics as well as gene ontology disrupted by all rare coding CNVs.
